title: Repairing a Damaged Main Shutoff Valve: Gate Valve Failure, Curb Stop, and Pipe-Freezing Methods

locations.name: Basement shutoff area (near water meter)
locations.basis: Transcript: 'go down to the basement to shut the water off' and 'next to the water meter there's the water main here.'

locations.name: Curb stop (municipal shutoff, street-side)
locations.basis: Transcript: 'curb stop' and description of town shutoff procedure that occurs outside the building.

summary: This Old House presents a practical sequence for addressing a damaged main shutoff valve. When the in-house gate valve spins and won’t move, the host explains how these valves operate and why wear at the valve stem can render them unusable. With access to the town curb stop often required, the segment then discusses external shutoff options and the rationale for isolating the line when internal valves fail. To perform a valve replacement without risking water damage, the video demonstrates two pipe-freezing approaches (a CO2 canister method and a refrigeration-based freezing tool) to hard-freeze a short section of pipe, allowing the old valve to be cut out and a new valve installed. The replacement highlighted is a ball valve (full-port stainless steel) with a solderless connection to speed installation and guard against backflow while the work is completed. The overall lesson blends problem diagnosis, municipal shutoff basics, and rapid, fire-safe valve replacement techniques suitable for both residential and larger-scale plumbing scenarios.

sections.title: Identify failed main shutoff valve (gate valve)
sections.description: The host reveals a spinning, stuck main shutoff valve—consistent with a gate valve whose stem threads have corroded or worn. He explains how a gate valve uses a bronze guillotine to seal and notes that wear can prevent the valve from moving up or down, signaling a failed shutoff.

sections.title: Municipal shutoffs and curb stop as alternative control
sections.description: The video describes the curb stop as the town-controlled shutoff located outside the building and explains how crews use a special wrench to shut it off when internal valves are compromised or inaccessible.

sections.title: Pipe freezing methods to isolate the line for valve work
concepts: freeze the pipe briefly to create an ice plug
sections.description: To safely replace the valve without letting water flow, the presenter introduces pipe-freezing techniques: first a CO2 canister freezes a short pipe section, then an alternative refrigeration-based freezing tool uses ultra-cold clamps to accomplish the same isolation, enabling valve replacement without soldering in a wet environment.

sections.title: Valve replacement options: ball valve and solderless connection
sections.description: After isolation, the team discusses replacing the damaged gate valve with a ball valve for easier operation. They highlight a full-port stainless steel ball valve and advocate using a solderless connection to speed installation and minimize issues with soldering in a damp environment.
